description:
FOUND s499e (Opus, 2026-09-27) while probing #2380 (x{,2}+ row).

perl 5.40.3 vs PCL:
    print(("xx" =~ /^x{,2}$/) ? 1 : 0, ("x{,2}" =~ /^x{,2}$/) ? 1 : 0, "\n");
  perl: 10     PCL: 01

perl 5.34 added `{,n}` as a quantifier meaning `{0,n}` (perlre: "{,n}  Match at most n times"); also `{ 2 , 3 }` with blanks inside the braces is a quantifier since 5.34.  cl-ppcre reads `{,2}` as literal characters.  The compiler side (Pl::InterpScan, #237) already classifies `{,3}` and `{ 2, 3 }` as quantifiers.

FIX SHAPE: one arm in the runtime's rewrite scan (%pcl-rewrite-scan, which since #2380 recognises counted quantifiers in %pcl-rx-quantifier-end): outside a class, `{,n}` -> `{0,n}` and `{ n , m }` -> `{n,m}`; then extend %pcl-rx-quantifier-end so `x{,2}+` is possessive too.  Probe the literal cases perl keeps (`x{,}`, `x{a}`).
=== DONE (s499h) ===
%pcl-rx-counted-end = perl 5.34+'s counted-quantifier grammar ({,n} = {0,n}; blanks around numbers/comma); the one rewrite scan writes it blank-free behind a third pre-test (%pcl-has-loose-counted), so {,n}? and {,n}+ compose.  {,} {a} \{ and in-class stay literal.  17-row probe (scratch/s499h/q1.pl) = perl.  Guard Pl/t/regexp-subst-01.t row 51, inverse-verified.  Companion re/regexp.t re/pat.t re/pat_rt_report.t op/qr.t before = after (re_tests' {,2} rows sit past the #326 hang).  ir-spec Â§10-count.  Residue: #2471 (\N{3,4}).
subject: SILENT WRONG: perl 5.34+'s `{,n}` quantifier (`x{,2}` = `x{0,2}`) is matched as LITERAL text by cl-ppcre -- "xx" =~ /^x{,2}$/ is 1 in perl, 0 in PCL (and "x{,2}" matches)
